assessment: Gross margin above 60% in FY2026 — pricing power, not a commodity cost structure.
Net margin above 50% in FY2026 — unusually profitable even for a large-cap tech company.
Revenue grew at a 68% CAGR over FY2022-FY2026 — the growth is real but historically extreme, so it cannot be extrapolated safely.
Net cash of $40.7bn at FY2026 year-end (cash + marketable securities minus debt) — no solvency concern on the balance sheet.
FY2023 revenue was almost flat (+0.2%) and operating cash flow fell — the business is cyclical, not a straight line up.

moat_assessment: Scale + switching costs: data-centre customers build systems, software (CUDA) and models around NVIDIA's platform; changing supplier means re-engineering, which is why gross margin stayed above 70% in FY2026.
R&D engine: R&D spend rose from $5.3bn (FY2022) to $18.5bn (FY2026), a 37% CAGR — the moat is funded every year, not a one-off patent.

Counterweight: that moat is tied to one demand wave (AI data-centre spending). FY2023 shows the cycle: revenue growth slowed to 0.2% and operating cash flow fell, before the AI wave lifted FY2024-FY2026.
competitive_risks: Customer concentration risk is real in this industry (a few hyperscalers buy most data-centre GPUs) — but the exact share is not in the XBRL facts pulled here, so it is flagged, not quantified.
Competitors (AMD, custom silicon from cloud customers) attack the same market; no peer financials were pulled in this project, so no head-to-head margin comparison is claimed.
not_available: Segment revenue split (Compute & Networking vs Graphics) — not present in the SEC company-facts file used here.
Total addressable market size / market share — no independent source was pulled; not estimated.
Peer financials — no peer filings were pulled in this project.
industry.conclusion: A dominant position in a fast-growing but cyclical market: revenue CAGR 68% (FY2022-FY2026), gross margin 71.1% in FY2026, funded by R&D that itself compounds. The moat looks real, but it is a single-wave moat — the FY2023 slowdown is the reminder.

assumptions.fcf_base: FY2026 free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capex)

risks.risk: Valuation risk — the price already assumes a lot of growth
risks.evidence: At $128.80 (as of Nov 20, 2026 5:05 PM ET), the share price is 49% above this project's DCF base case ($86.72). The DCF only reaches the current price if FCF grows well above 12% a year or the discount rate is well below 10%.

risks.risk: Demand cyclicality — the AI wave can pause, as it did in FY2023
risks.evidence: Revenue growth was 0.2% in FY2023 and operating cash flow fell from $9.1bn (FY2022) to $5.6bn (FY2023). A pause in data-centre spending would hit revenue, margins and FCF at once.

A few hyperscale customers buy most data-centre GPUs. The exact share is not in the XBRL facts pulled here, so it is flagged qualitatively, not quantified. Losing or delaying one large customer matters.
AMD competes directly, and large cloud customers design their own AI chips. No peer financials were pulled, so this is a qualitative risk; the defence is R&D spend, which rose to $18.5bn in FY2026.
US export controls on advanced chips to China are a known, recurring risk for NVIDIA. This project does not estimate the revenue at stake.
Shares outstanding fell from 24.64bn (FY2024) to 24.30bn (FY2026) — buybacks more than offset dilution over this window, but that depends on buybacks continuing.

bear_case.assumptions: FCF growth 8% (vs 12% base), discount rate 11% (vs 10%), terminal growth 2% (vs 3%)
bear_case.story: AI data-centre spending pauses for a year, growth slows, and investors demand a higher return for the risk. FCF still grows, but the price paid today would be well above even a cautious fair value.

investment_analyst.final_judgement: Strong business, demanding price. At $128.80 the market price is above even the top of this DCF sensitivity range ($69.25-$118.03), and 49% above the base case ($86.72). The business would have to grow faster than the 12% FCF growth assumed here — or be discounted at less than 10% — for the current price to equal the DCF value.
what_the_business_does_well: Revenue CAGR 68% (FY2022-FY2026) with a 71.1% gross margin.
Free cash flow of $96.7bn in FY2026, a 45% FCF margin.
Net cash of $40.7bn — the balance sheet is not the risk.
what_would_change_the_judgement: FCF growth sustained at about 22% a year for 5 years (vs 12% in the base case, at the same 10% discount rate) would be needed for the DCF to reach the current price — even 16% growth only gives $101.39 a share.
A data-centre spending pause (the FY2023 pattern) would cut the DCF sharply — see the Bear Case.
A lower discount rate (e.g. if rates fall) lifts every DCF value in the sensitivity table.
